Thanks Marissa

Quick set of items from our legal/regulatory review (attached annotated redline and a short question list):

1) Controller/Processor: please confirm Redwood's view of roles. Our starting position is Acme is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor for the POC and any hosted deployment.

2) Subprocessors: please provide a current list and confirm how you notify customers of additions. Can Redwood accept a provision that material changes require 30 days' notice?

3) Breach notice timing: we typically negotiate for an obligation to notify "without undue delay and no later than 72 hours." Can Redwood accept that language?

4) Data residency: for production we require EU residency (data at rest and logs). For the POC we are OK in US region if a migration path exists. What's the recommended path and timeline to move to EU?

5) Logs & retention: we need clarity on what logs are retained, for how long (app logs, request/response logs, KV caches) and whether PII is redacted. We'd like a 90-day retention window for full logs and a confirmation that we can request deletion of full-records.

6) Deletion & audit: describe the process and timing once Acme requests data deletion. Do you provide attestations?

Attached: acme_dpa_redline_annotated.pdf, dpa_questions.docx

Can you loop in legal and security and send back proposed language? We may want a short legal-to-legal call next week.

Alyssa

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA clarifications / data handling follow-up

Marissa

Comments / proposed responses below (draft for legal/security review):

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood accepts Processor role for hosted and dedicated deployments. We will sign the DPA recognizing Acme as Controller and Redwood as Processor for customer data processed via the service.

2) Subprocessors: we maintain a public subprocessor list at https://redwood.ai/security/subprocessors.csv. Standard practice: notify customers of additions via email at least 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor; we can commit to that for material changes.

3) Breach notice: our security team recommends the industry standard wording: "We will notify the Controller without undue delay and, where feasible, no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach that is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons." This is operationally achievable; we should confirm with infra on detection windows but security is comfortable with the 72-hour timeline for initial notification.

4) Data residency: we support region pinning for production and can provision EU-hosted deployments (requires Dedicated or Private deployment for guaranteed residency). For POC in hosted, we can run in US but propose a migration plan to EU within X weeks once contract is in place.

5) Logs & retention: default request/response and telemetry logs are retained for 30 days in hosted by default. We can offer a 90-day retention for logs as a contract parameter for Enterprise/Dedicated customers; note that full-response logging (request+response) is considered data that must be handled per retention/deletion requests. Backups are retained up to 180 days for disaster recovery. PII redaction: we offer payload redaction tooling; customers can enable automatic redaction or request suppression of response logging.

6) Deletion & audit: upon Controller request we will delete customer data from primary stores within 30 days and from backups within 90-180 days depending on the backup window. We can provide an attestation of deletion and coordinate an audit or written confirmation for enterprise customers.

I attached a short draft response you can send to Acme (internal_dpa_response_draft.txt). Recommend legal/security sign-off and then a legal-to-legal call with Acme to go through open items and timeline.

Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Platform Security | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.ai

Alyssa

Thanks for the detailed notes and annotated redline. I looped in our security and legal folks and pasted a short summary of proposed positions below; attaching the draft response as well.

- Roles: Redwood confirms we operate as Processor and accept Acme as Controller for data processed in the service.
- Subprocessors: current list: https://redwood.ai/security/subprocessors.csv. We will notify you of material additions; standard notice is 30 days.
- Breach notice: proposed language "We will notify the Controller without undue delay and, where feasible, no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons."
- Data residency: For guaranteed EU data residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment; we can support a migration plan from POC (US) to EU provisioning once the contract is executed — estimated provisioning timeline to confirm on the call.
- Logs & retention: default hosted retention is 30 days. We can contractually provide 90-day retention for request/response logs for enterprise agreements; backups retained up to 180 days. PII redaction tooling is available.
- Deletion: primary-store deletion within 30 days from receipt; backups purged per backup lifecycle (up to 180 days). We can provide deletion attestations for enterprise customers.

Next steps: would you and your legal team be available for a short legal-to-legal call to finalize DPA language? I'm proposing Mon, 22 Feb 2026 at 10:00 AM PT (please confirm or suggest alternatives). I've attached our draft response for your review.

Thanks — look forward to closing this out.
